quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Engine braking means shifting to a lower gear to slow down. This produces a braking effect similar to using the brakes.

questions.question: What is true about approved helmets?

options.text: They can limit your side view.
They allow you to see as far to the sides as you need.
You do not have to wear them if you think they limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: They allow you to see as far to the sides as you need.
questions.explanation: Approved helmets do not limit your field of vision in a dangerous way. They allow you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, where should you ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
In the lane to their left.
In the far right part of the lane.
Behind the right tire of their vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors. Being visible in the rearview mirror increases your chances of being seen.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your eyes focused on the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look ahead through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and do not use it again.
Release the front brake and then squeeze it hard.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely and right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: Should your following distance be different at night than during the day?

options.text: Yes, you should allow more distance at night.
No, you should allow less distance at night.
No, you should always use the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should allow more distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distances because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. You should allow a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: When will a helmet not give you the best protection?

options.text: If it is certified by the DOT.
If it is free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: If it has cracks.
questions.explanation: Your helmet should be certified by the DOT and fit snugly all the way around. It must be free of any damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps to protect you properly.

questions.question: What is true about making eye contact with other drivers?

options.text: It is the best way to know they see you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not register that they are there.

questions.question: If your motorcycle wobbles, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will stop on its own.
Slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce speed by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible and check what caused the wobble.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the paint.
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection should include tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a full inspection before every ride. Paint condition is not part of a safety inspection.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean the driver will yield to you safely.
The driver will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean the driver will yield to you safely.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact as proof that a driver will yield. Many drivers look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on your motorcycle?

options.text: Lean with you as you turn.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you turn.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with the rider during turns. They should sit as close to the front as possible without crowding the rider and hold firmly onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black text or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which color makes you most visible when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: What type of footwear best protects your feet while riding?

options.text: Sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots to protect and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they do not catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they do not get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It supplies at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, what should you do?

options.text: Ride straight across the tracks while staying in your lane.
Turn to cross the tracks straight.
Do not try to cross on a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks while staying in your lane.
questions.explanation: Cross angled railroad tracks by riding straight ahead in your lane. Do not turn to cross at a 90-degree angle—this could force you into another lane of traffic.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they use their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center of the lane. The driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors. This position helps the driver see you.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Only use their mirrors to see other vehicles.
Turn their head to check for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to check for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you use a sidecar to carry a load, what should you do?

options.text: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
Put the load in the seat without securing it.
Secure the load at the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so its weight does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not shift and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place loads toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles from other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, how much stopping distance do motorcycles need?
questions.correctAnswerText: The same as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, motorcycles need as much distance to stop as cars do.
